question: 'Baisakhi' marks the beginning of the Solar New Year and is celebrated under different regional names across India. Which of the following correctly matches the regional name with its state?
option_1: Poila Boishakh - West Bengal; Bohag Bihu - Assam; Vishu - Kerala; Puthandu - Tamil Nadu
option_2: Poila Boishakh - Assam; Bohag Bihu - West Bengal; Vishu - Tamil Nadu; Puthandu - Kerala
option_3: Poila Boishakh - Odisha; Bohag Bihu - Kerala; Vishu - Assam; Puthandu - West Bengal
option_4: All four names refer to the same festival celebrated only in Punjab
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poila Boishakh - West Bengal; Bohag Bihu - Assam; Vishu - Kerala; Puthandu - Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baisakhi (Vaisakhi) marks the beginning of the Solar New Year; for Sikhs, it also commemorates the day Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth.

 

• While known as Baisakhi in Punjab, the same solar transition is celebrated as Poila Boishakh in West Bengal, Bohag Bihu in Assam, Vishu in Kerala, and Puthandu in Tamil Nadu.

 

• This is a classic example of a single astronomical/agricultural event being marked under different regional names and traditions across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, Ugadi (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana), Yugadi (Karnataka) and Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra/Goa) all mark the same New Year day, based on the Hindu month of Chaitra.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2 and 3 incorrectly swap the state-name pairings.

 

• Option 4 is factually wrong, as these are distinct regional names, not all confined to Punjab.

question: The Kumbh Mela, held at four sacred locations in India, was inscribed by UNESCO on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in which year, and how frequently is the 'Maha Kumbh' held at Prayagraj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2017; Every 144 years (12 Purna Kumbhs).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kumbh Mela was inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.

 

• The Maha Kumbh is held every 144 years (after 12 Purna Kumbhs), and only at Prayagraj.

 

• The Purna Kumbh, held every 12 years, rotates among four locations: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and Ujjain.

 

• Prayagraj's Kumbh is held at the Triveni Sangam, the meeting point of the Ganges, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mythologically, these four sites mark where drops of Amrit (nectar of immortality) fell during the Samudra Manthan (churning of the ocean) between gods and demons.

 

• The Ujjain Kumbh (Simhastha) is held on the banks of the Shipra River.

 

NOTE

 

• 2015, 2019 and 2010, and the other frequency claims (Options 1, 3, 4), do not correctly match the documented UNESCO inscription year (2017) or the Maha Kumbh's 144-year cycle.

question: In the Jagannath Rath Yatra at Puri, the chariots of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are respectively named Nandighosa, Taladhwaja and Darpadalana. How many wheels does each of these chariots have?
option_4: All three chariots have an equal number of 14 wheels
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nandighosa-16, Taladhwaja-14, Darpadalana-12.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Jagannath Rath Yatra, held in Puri, is considered the oldest and largest chariot festival in the world.

 

• Nandighosa, the chariot of Jagannath, has 16 wheels; Taladhwaja, the chariot of Balabhadra (his elder brother), has 14 wheels; and Darpadalana, the chariot of Subhadra (his younger sister), has 12 wheels.

 

• The deities travel from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple (their aunt's abode), staying there for nine days before the Bahuda Yatra (return journey).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A ceremonial grand bath (Snana Yatra) of the deities is performed before the Rath Yatra begins.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 incorrectly rearrange or equalise the wheel counts; the correct, distinct counts are 16, 14 and 12 respectively.

question: 'Durga Puja in Kolkata' was inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in which year, and which event commemorates the victory of Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021; Vijaya Dashami (Dussehra).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Durga Puja in Kolkata' was inscribed by UNESCO on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021.

 

• Durga Puja commemorates the victory of Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura; this victory is culminated and celebrated on Vijaya Dashami (Dussehra), marking the end of the 10-day Navratri/Durga Puja period.

 

• Mahalaya marks the beginning of the Durga Puja season, when the eyes of the clay idols are ceremonially painted to bring the goddess to life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other West Bengal festivals include Pohela Boishakh (Bengali New Year) and the Gangasagar Mela.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahalaya (Option 1) marks the beginning, not the culmination, of Durga Puja.

 

• Durga Ashtami and Kalbaisakhi (Options 3, 4) are not correctly linked with the specific UNESCO inscription year or the Mahishasura victory culmination event.

question: The public celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi as a grand community event, rather than a private household ritual, is credited to which freedom fighter, who revived it in 1893?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ganesh Chaturthi, dedicated to Ganesha and observed on Shukla Paksha Chaturthi of the Hindu month of Bhadrapada, had been celebrated since the Satavahana Dynasty era as a private household ritual.

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak revived its public celebration in 1893, transforming it into a grand public event to bridge the gap between Brahmins and non-Brahmins and foster nationalist unity under British rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This strategic use of religious festivals for social and political mobilisation is a recurring theme in India's freedom movement, alongside Tilak's promotion of Shivaji Jayanti.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi, V. D. Savarkar and Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Options 1, 3, 4) were significant freedom movement figures but are not credited with reviving Ganesh Chaturthi's public celebration; that credit specifically belongs to Tilak.

question: 'Onam', the harvest festival of Kerala famous for the Vallam Kali (snake boat races) on the Pampa River, is celebrated to mark the annual homecoming of which mythological figure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is King Mahabali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Onam, Kerala's major harvest festival, is celebrated to mark the homecoming of (King) Mahabali.

 

• It is famous for the traditional boat race, Vallam Kali, especially the grand snake boat races on the Pampa River.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vishu, another major Kerala festival, is celebrated as the Malayalam New Year.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Krishna (Option 2) is central to Janmashtami celebrations, not Onam.

 

• Lord Ayyappa (Option 3) is the presiding deity of the Sabarimala and Makaravilakku festivals.

 

• Sage Agastya (Option 4) has no documented association with the Onam homecoming legend in the notes.

question: 'Pongal', the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, includes a day dedicated to the worship of cattle and the celebration of Jallikattu (bull-taming sport). Which day of Pongal is this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Day 3 - Mattu Pongal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pongal is a four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu expressing gratitude to the Surya (Sun), nature and cattle.

 

• Day 3, Mattu Pongal, is dedicated to the worship of cattle for their role in agriculture, and it is on this day that Jallikattu (bull-taming sport) is traditionally celebrated.

 

• Day 1 (Bhogi Pongal) involves cleansing homes and burning old items; Day 2 (Thai Pongal) is the main day, offering the Pongal dish to the Sun God; Day 4 (Kaanum Pongal) involves family reunions and social visits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jallikattu, associated with Mattu Pongal, has been a subject of significant legal and cultural debate in Tamil Nadu regarding animal welfare regulations.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhogi, Thai and Kaanum Pongal (Options 1, 2, 4) are the other three days of Pongal, each with distinct rituals unrelated to cattle worship and Jallikattu.

question: The 'Hornbill Festival', known as the 'Festival of Festivals' and the largest cultural festival of Northeast India, is held annually at which venue in Nagaland, and during which dates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kisama Heritage Village; 1 to 10 December.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hornbill Festival, the largest cultural festival of Northeast India, is known as the 'Festival of Festivals', held at the Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village).

 

• It is celebrated annually from 1 December to 10 December; 1 December also marks Nagaland Statehood Day.

 

• It was first organised by the Government of Nagaland in 2000, and is named after the Great Hornbill, symbolising boldness and prosperity in Naga folklore.

 

• All 17 major Naga tribes (Angami, Ao, Konyak, Sumi, Lotha, etc.) participate, featuring war dances, folk songs, and the bamboo dance (Zeliang).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Note: The Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival is a distinct festival celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh, not to be confused with Nagaland's Hornbill Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 incorrectly state the venue and/or dates; the correct venue and dates are specifically Kisama Heritage Village and 1-10 December.

question: 'Kharchi Puja', also known as the 'Festival of Fourteen Gods', is a major festival of Tripura primarily linked with the worship of indigenous tribal deities. How many deities are specifically associated with this festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kharchi Puja, also known as the 'Festival of Fourteen Gods', is a major festival of Tripura, associated with 14 deities.

 

• It is primarily linked with the worship of indigenous tribal deities, reflecting Tripura's distinct tribal-religious heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Tripura festivals include the Garia Carnival (dedicated to Lord Garia, deity of wealth, livestock and prosperity, conducted under the guidance of a tribal priest called Ochai) and the Biju (Bizu) Festival, celebrated by the Chakma community.

 

NOTE

 

• 12, 15 and 16 (Options 1, 3, 4) do not correspond to the correct number of deities (14) associated with Kharchi Puja.

question: 'Chapchar Kut', also known as the 'Festival of Happiness', is a major festival of Mizoram celebrated after the completion of which agricultural activity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clearing forests for Jhum (shifting) cultivation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chapchar Kut, also known as the 'Festival of Happiness', is celebrated after the completion of clearing forests for Jhum (shifting) cultivation in Mizoram.

 

• The Cheraw (bamboo) dance is prominently performed during this festival, alongside various other cultural performances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Mizo 'Kut' (festival) traditions include Pawl Kut (the 'Straw Festival'), Thalfavang Kut (an autumn festival) and Mim Kut.

 

NOTE

 

• Harvesting of rice, sowing of maize and threshing of paddy (Options 1, 3, 4) are agricultural activities associated with other specific festivals (such as Mim Kut for maize harvest), not the forest-clearing activity marked by Chapchar Kut.

question: 'Mim Kut', a post-harvest festival of Mizoram, is celebrated after the harvesting of which crop, symbolising survival and love as the 'last harvest'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maize (corn).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mim Kut is a post-harvest festival celebrated after the harvesting of maize (corn) in Mizoram.

 

• 'Mim' means Maize, representing the last harvest, symbolising survival and love; 'Kut' means Festival in the Mizo language.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This festival reflects the deep connection between Mizoram's agricultural cycle (particularly Jhum cultivation) and its cultural celebrations, as also seen in Chapchar Kut.

 

NOTE

 

• Rice, wheat and millet (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the crop specifically associated with Mim Kut; the notes specifically identify maize as the crop marking this 'last harvest' festival.

question: During the 'Solung Festival' of the Adi tribe in Arunachal Pradesh, which traditional rice-based drink is shared to promote social bonding?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apong.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the Solung Festival, celebrated by the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, 'Apong' (a traditional rice drink) is shared to promote social bonding.

 

• Solung marks the end of the sowing season and the beginning of the harvest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Adi tribe traditions include the Popir dance (tribute to goddess Mopin Ane, actually associated with the Galo tribe's Mopin festival) and Ponung dance, performed by Adi women to ensure a bountiful harvest.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhang (Option 1) is a traditional fermented drink of the Himalayan/Tibetan regions, Thukpa (Option 3) is a noodle soup, and Soma (Option 4) is a ritual drink referenced in ancient Vedic texts — none of these is the specific drink associated with Solung.

question: During 'Nuakhai', a post-harvest thanksgiving festival of Odisha celebrating the arrival of the season's first rice (Nabanna), the new rice is first offered to which deity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maa Samaleswari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nuakhai is a post-harvest thanksgiving festival of Odisha, celebrated to welcome the first rice of the season.

 

• The Nabanna (new rice) is first offered to Maa Samaleswari, a prominent regional deity worshipped especially in the Sambalpur region of Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Odisha festivals include Raja Parba (honouring womanhood and fertility) and Dhanu Jatra (recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's largest open-air theatre, held in Bargarh).

 

NOTE

 

• Maa Mangala, Maa Bhubaneswari and Maa Budhi Thakurani (Options 2, 3, 4) are other regional deities of Odisha, but the Nabanna offering during Nuakhai is specifically made to Maa Samaleswari.

question: 'Medaram Jatara' (Sammakka Saralamma Jatara), often called the 'Kumbh Mela of the South' and considered Asia's largest tribal congregation, commemorates a 13th-century revolt led by Sammakka and her daughter Saralamma against which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kakatiya Dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Medaram Jatara, celebrated once every two years in the sacred forest of Mulugu District, Telangana, is often called the 'Kumbh Mela of the South' and is considered Asia's largest tribal congregation.

 

• It commemorates a 13th-century revolt led by Sammakka and her daughter Saralamma against the Kakatiya dynasty rulers, honouring them as tribal goddesses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Telangana festivals include Bonalu (dedicated to Goddess Mahakali, declared an official state festival in 2014) and Bathukamma (a floral festival honouring Goddess Gauri/Parvati).

 

NOTE

 

• Chola Dynasty, Vijayanagara Empire and Chalukya Dynasty (Options 1, 3, 4) are other major South Indian dynasties, but the historical revolt commemorated by Medaram Jatara was specifically against the Kakatiya Dynasty.

question: 'Mahamastakabhisheka', the most significant Jain festival held once every 12 years at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka, involves the ceremonial anointment of a 57-foot statue of which figure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahubali, son of Rishabhanatha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahamastakabhisheka, the most significant Jain festival, is held once every 12 years at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka.

 

• The ceremony involves the ceremonial anointment of the 57-foot (17.4 m) statue of Bahubali, son of the first Jain Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, which stands atop Vindhyagiri Hill.

 

• The statue was commissioned in 981 AD by the Western Ganga Dynasty, and the festival was last celebrated in February 2018.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other significant Karnataka festivals include the Hampi Festival (celebrating the Vijayanagara Empire's heritage) and the Pattadakal Festival (celebrating the Chalukya Dynasty's architectural legacy at the UNESCO World Heritage Pattadakal Group of Monuments).

 

NOTE

 

• Rishabhanatha, Mahavira and Parshvanatha (Options 1, 2, 4) are important Jain Tirthankaras, but the specific 57-foot statue honoured at Mahamastakabhisheka is of Bahubali, Rishabhanatha's son.

question: 'Kambala', a traditional sporting event held annually in the coastal districts of Karnataka, is associated with which activity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buffalo racing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kambala is a traditional buffalo race held annually in the coastal districts of Karnataka, deeply rooted in the region's agrarian culture.

 

• It is typically held in paddy fields filled with mud and water, with pairs of buffaloes racing while guided by a runner.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other unique Karnataka events include the Kadlekai Parishe (Groundnut Fair) and Yellamma Jatara, celebrated in honour of Goddess Yellamma in both Karnataka and Telangana.

 

NOTE

 

• Camel racing (Option 1) is more associated with events like the Pushkar Fair (though primarily a camel trading fair, not a race event as such), horse and elephant racing (Options 3, 4) are not documented as the activity associated with Kambala, which is specifically buffalo racing.

question: The 'Pushkar Camel Fair' (Pushkar Fair), one of the world's largest livestock fairs, is held in which state, and which two cities jointly celebrate the International Kite Festival mentioned alongside it in the notes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan; Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and Jaipur (Rajasthan).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pushkar Camel Fair, held in Pushkar, Rajasthan, is one of the world's largest livestock fairs, featuring processions of decorated camels and folk performances, coinciding with the desert climate's peak.

 

• The International Kite Festival is celebrated in Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and Jaipur (Rajasthan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan's Nagaur Cattle Fair is India's second-largest livestock fair, while the Sonepur Cattle Fair in Bihar holds the distinction of being the largest cattle fair in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat alone, and the other Rajasthan city pairs (Options 1, 3, 4) do not correctly identify the Pushkar Fair's state (Rajasthan) or the correct city pairing for the International Kite Festival.

question: 'Sonepur Cattle Fair' (Sonepur Mela), held at the confluence of the Ganges and Gandak rivers in Bihar, holds which distinction among Indian livestock fairs?
option_3: The only cattle fair exclusively for donkey trading
option_4: The smallest cattle fair in Eastern India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asia's largest cattle fair.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonepur Cattle Fair, held at the confluence of the Ganges and Gandak rivers in Sonepur, Bihar, is recognised as Asia's largest cattle fair.

 

• This is distinct from Rajasthan's Nagaur Cattle Fair, which is India's second-largest livestock fair, and Gujarat's Vautha Fair (known as 'Gujarat's Pushkar'), famous specifically for its donkey market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihar also hosts the Rajgir Mahotsav, showcasing classical and folk dance and music, and the Vaishali Mahotsav, commemorating the birth anniversary of Mahavira.

 

NOTE

 

• 'India's second-largest' (Option 1) describes Rajasthan's Nagaur Cattle Fair, not Sonepur. Options 3 and 4 do not correctly describe Sonepur's actual standing as Asia's largest cattle fair.

question: 'Gangaur', a festival celebrated in parts of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, honours which divine couple, with married women praying for their husbands' long life and unmarried girls seeking a similar partner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gauri (Parvati) and Shiva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gangaur, celebrated across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, is celebrated to honour Gauri (Parvati) and Shiva.

 

• Married women pray for the long life of their husbands, while unmarried girls seek a virtuous life partner like Shiva.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan hosts several other notable fairs, including the Karni Mata Fair (held twice a year during Navratri) and the Ajmer Sharif Urs, one of India's largest spiritual gatherings.

 

NOTE

 

• Radha-Krishna, Lakshmi-Vishnu and Sita-Rama (Options 1, 3, 4) are other significant divine pairs in Hindu tradition, but Gangaur is specifically dedicated to the worship of Gauri and Shiva.

question: 'Bhagoria', a festival celebrated across Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan, begins seven days before which major Hindu festival, and is famously known as a 'matchmaking' fair?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Holika Dahan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhagoria, celebrated across Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan, begins seven days before Holika Dahan.

 

• It is famously known as a 'matchmaking' fair, where young men and women choose life partners; the name derives from 'Bhag' (to run), referencing the tradition of couples eloping and later receiving formal family acceptance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhagoria is closely associated with the Bhil tribal community, India's largest tribal group, and is celebrated primarily in the tribal belts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Diwali, Navratri and Makar Sankranti (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the festival before which Bhagoria specifically begins; that is Holika Dahan.

question: 'Bastar Dussehra', celebrated in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh and renowned as the world's longest festival spanning 75 days, is dedicated to which presiding deity of Bastar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Danteshwari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bastar Dussehra, celebrated in the Bastar district of Chhattisgarh, is renowned as the world's longest festival, spanning 75 days.

 

• It is dedicated to Danteshwari, the presiding deity of Bastar.

 

• The festival was initiated by Maharaja Purushottam Dev of the Kakatiya Dynasty in the 15th century (1408 AD).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Chhattisgarh festivals include the Goncha Festival (featuring the Tupki, a bamboo mock gun using goncha fruit as bullets) and the Karma Festival, dedicated to Karam Devta.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahakali (Option 2) is the deity honoured through Telangana's Bonalu festival; Sammakka (Option 3) is honoured at Telangana's Medaram Jatara; Karni Mata (Option 4) is honoured at Rajasthan's Karni Mata Fair — none is the presiding deity of Bastar Dussehra.

question: 'Attukal Pongala', which entered the Guinness World Records for the largest gathering of women for a religious activity, is presided over by which deity, an incarnation of Bhadrakali?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Attukal Bhagavathy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Attukal Pongala, held in Kerala, entered the Guinness World Records for the largest gathering of women for a religious activity.

 

• The main ritual is performed only by women, and the presiding deity is Attukal Bhagavathy, an incarnation of Bhadrakali.

 

• Kappukettu marks the beginning of the festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala's Sabarimala Festival, dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, was historically marked by restrictions on women of menstruating age (10-50 years), which the Supreme Court of India lifted in 2018.

 

NOTE

 

• Kamakhya (Option 2) is worshipped at Assam's Ambubachi Mela, Mariamman (Option 3) is honoured through Tamil Nadu's Karakattam dance, and Samaleswari (Option 4) receives the Nabanna offering during Odisha's Nuakhai — none of these is Attukal Pongala's presiding deity.

question: In which year did the Supreme Court of India lift the earlier restriction barring women of menstruating age (10-50 years) from entering the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala, dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, women of menstrual age (10-50 years) were historically restricted from entry.

 

• The Supreme Court of India lifted this restriction in 2018, in a landmark judgment on gender equality and religious practice.

 

• Makaravilakku, another festival celebrated at the same temple, is also dedicated to Lord Ayyappa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This judgment remains one of the most significant and debated Supreme Court rulings concerning the intersection of religious customs and constitutional rights in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2016, 2017 and 2019 (Options 1, 2, 4) do not correspond to the correct year (2018) of the Supreme Court's Sabarimala verdict.

question: 'Ambubachi Mela', held at the Kamakhya Temple in Assam and known as the 'Kumbh Mela of the East', celebrates which annual event associated with Goddess Kamakhya, symbolising the fertility of Mother Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Her annual menstruation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ambubachi Mela, held at the Kamakhya Temple in Assam, is known as the 'Kumbh Mela of the East'.

 

• It celebrates the annual menstruation of Goddess Kamakhya, symbolising the fertility of Mother Earth.

 

• This theme parallels Odisha's Raja Parba, which similarly celebrates the menstruation of Bhudevi (Mother Earth) and honours womanhood and fertility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Assam festivals include the Majuli Festival (on the banks of the Brahmaputra) and Me Dam Me Phi, celebrated by the Tai Ahom community in honour of ancestral and heavenly deities.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 do not correctly describe the specific event (menstruation, symbolising fertility) celebrated during Ambubachi Mela.

question: 'Bathukamma', a floral festival of Telangana whose name means 'Mother, come alive', involves placing an idol of Parvati/Gauri made of which material at the top of the floral stack?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Turmeric, called Gouramma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Bathukamma, an idol of Parvati or Gauri, made of turmeric and called Gouramma, is placed at the top of the floral stack.

 

• Each evening, women gather in circles around their Bathukammas to sing traditional folk songs, clap rhythmically, and dance together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bonalu, another major Telangana festival dedicated to Goddess Mahakali, dates back to 1813, when people prayed to the goddess for the city's safety after a devastating plague in Hyderabad and Secunderabad; it was declared an official State festival in 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• Sandalwood, clay and silver (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the material used for the Gouramma idol in Bathukamma; the notes specifically identify turmeric.
